nodes.name: One-pot GO synthesis
nodes.procedure: Rapid one-pot method to prepare single-layer GO using in-situ intercalation of graphite with K2FeO4. The obtained FeO₄²⁻ and atomic oxygen act as oxidants to ensure the exfoliation. Then the concentrated sulfuric acid and oxidants intercalate into the layers of graphite to form intercalated graphite oxide (GIO).
nodes.source_text: Peng et al. established a rapid one-pot method to prepare single-layer GO using in-situ intercalation of graphite with K₂FeO₄... intercalated graphite oxide (GIO)

nodes.name: FeCl3-GIC vapor intercalation
nodes.procedure: FeCl3-GICs prepared by melting FeCl3 in a sealed space, thereby driving molecular vapor to be inserted into the graphite layer.
nodes.source_text: Wang et al. have successfully prepared the FeCl₃-GICs by melting FeCl₃ in a sealed space, thereby driving molecular vapor to be inserted into the graphite layer

nodes.name: FeCl3-FLG ultrasonication
nodes.procedure: Few-layer graphene intercalated with FeCl3 (FeCl3-FLG) through ultra-sonication treatment.
nodes.source_text: Qi et al. have also prepared few-layer graphene intercalated with FeCl₃ (FeCl₃-FLG) through ultra-sonication treatment

nodes.name: Exfoliation-recombination Mn oxide
nodes.procedure: Precursor of H-type layered manganese oxide (H-BirMO) was exfoliated in aqueous tetramethylammonium hydroxide (TMAOH) solution, and then Mn²⁺-BirMO and MnO₂-BirMO layered materials were fabricated by a recombination process followed by heat treatment.

nodes.name: Ion exchange LiMnO2
nodes.procedure: Layered LiMnO2 prepared through typical ion exchange method from layered NaMnO2.
nodes.source_text: Armstrong et al. have successfully prepared layered LiMnO₂ through typical ion exchange method from layered NaMnO₂

nodes.name: Sol-gel K-V2O5
nodes.procedure: In the first stage of sol-gel process, the α-V₂O₅ was decomposed with the presence of K⁺ ion in the aqueous solution, leading to the formation of intermediate δ-KₓV₂O₅·nH₂O phase. After hydrothermal treatment, the positions of K⁺ ions and water molecules in δ-KₓV₂O₅·nH₂O were further rearranged to establish a bilayered structure with an interlayer spacing of 9.62 Å.
